I118.summary_en: Describes a mining-algorithm-based psychological early warning system that helps college students identify suicide risk through a series of questions and answers, also usable by teachers and parents. No data, algorithm details or results are reported.

I119.summary_en: Identifies factors associated with self-reported depression among university students in Bangladesh using surveys on academic stress, lifestyle and social relationships, SMOTE and six supervised classifiers. Feature importance and LIME highlight suicidal ideation, social stress and academic burden.

I120.summary_en: Builds early warning models for depression and anxiety risk using academic, demographic, campus involvement and digital activity data from a large public university, applying classification, clustering and neural networks. Random Forest achieves 81% accuracy, and clustering reveals patterns of academic struggle, social isolation and addictive digital behavior.

I121.summary_en: Builds an SVM model to detect and warn of psychological abnormalities in college students from online questionnaire data, selecting six attributes by correlation. The SVM reaches 95% accuracy, outperforming other methods.

I122.summary_en: Proposes a big-data health monitoring and early warning model for college students based on body indicators (obesity, fat, muscle, edema). It does not address mental health or report results.

I123.summary_en: Presents PEACE, a web tool that uses machine learning to match college students with counsellors according to their mental health needs. No data or results are described; the article is retracted.

I124.screening_reason: mental health platform without data analytics or AI
I124.summary_en: Describes the design of the "Help Your Heart" mental health platform for university students, with psychological assessments and emotional intervention features. User feedback supports its usefulness; no analytics or AI are used.

I125.summary_en: Proposes an AI-driven conversational agent framework with enhanced NLP for emotional support and psychological well-being, framed within education and mental health services. No data, evaluation or results are reported.

I126.screening_reason: no analytics or AI described; includes teachers
I126.summary_en: Proposes a smartphone application for students and teachers with distress detection, academic misconduct detection and well-being support. Over 56% of evaluators rated the application as highly convenient.

I127.summary_en: Proposes a predictive model fusing EEG signals with clinical and other health variables to forecast risk of mental illness in patients. It reports 96% accuracy, higher than conventional approaches.

I128.summary_en: Identifies predictors of suicide in 27,014 college students using mental health indicators, impulsivity, sleep, internet addiction and sociodemographic variables, through exploratory analysis, correlation and several algorithms including a weighted Random Forest. Higher mental health indicator scores are significantly associated with suicidal behavior.

I129.summary_en: Detects depressive tendencies in 1,585 students from 38 higher education institutions in Quezon Province (Philippines) using demographic and self-report data and six supervised models. LightGBM performs best (94% accuracy, AUC 0.97); living arrangement, family type and academic program are key predictors.

I130.summary_en: Describes a big-data system for analysing physical health monitoring data of higher vocational students. It does not address mental health or report results.

I131.summary_en: Proposes sports health management strategies for universities from a sports data perspective, given the physical decline of Chinese college students. It does not address mental health or report analytic results.

I132.screening_reason: physical fitness and academic performance, not mental health
I132.summary_en: Analyses the relationship between physical fitness and academic performance in 44,240 Chinese undergraduates (2015-2019) using Apriori and Random Forest. Higher fitness is associated with better academic performance, with gender differences.

I133.best_result: Logistic Regression and SVM accuracy 96.6%, F1 0.964
I133.summary_en: Evaluates six classifiers to detect anxiety and depression in 142 undergraduates from a rural engineering institution in Maharashtra (India) using a 20-item Likert questionnaire. Logistic Regression and SVM perform best (96.6% accuracy, F1 0.964).

I134.summary_en: Presents a centralized digital framework combining anonymized wellness surveys, educational outcomes and engagement metrics for early identification of at-risk students, piloted with 500 students. The ensemble predictor reaches 87.3% accuracy and intervention response time drops from 48 to under 6 hours.

I135.screening_reason: general student health, not specifically mental health
I135.summary_en: Reviews the use of machine learning for health issues of schoolchildren and college students and the outcomes of these approaches. Mental health focus and review scope are not specified.

I136.summary_en: Analyses college physical health test data with the C4.5 decision tree and Pearson and Spearman correlations. Grade and gender are decisive factors, and industry-characteristic majors are positively associated with vital capacity and running.

I137.screening_reason: experimental intervention without data analytics or ML
I137.summary_en: Evaluates a 4-month aerobics and psychological guidance intervention in 60 female college students with mobile phone addiction using a quasi-experimental design. The intervention significantly reduces phone addiction, anxiety and depression (p < 0.01).

I138.summary_en: Applies educational data mining to predict academic results, framed as linked to youth depression, comparing six classifiers on academic, personal and family factors. No quantitative results are reported.

I139.screening_reason: mixed population of students and employees
I139.summary_en: Proposes a machine learning system using DASS-21 and behavioral and physiological indicators to detect stress in students and emotions in employees, with alerts and interventions. No data or results are reported.

I140.best_result: RF and SVM 100% on all metrics
I140.summary_en: Compares Random Forest, KNN and SVM for detecting academic stress in 275 university students using sociodemographic data and the PSS-14. RF and SVM reach 100% on all metrics and KNN 92.77% accuracy.

I141.summary_en: Discusses the ethical implications of AI-supported educational decisions about students, including data bias, continuous monitoring and effects on self-esteem and belonging. It proposes transparent governance frameworks without empirical analysis.

I142.screening_reason: empirical study without explicit ML; general review
I142.summary_en: Combines an empirical study of 1,147 students in Istanbul with a review of ML applications in mental health to examine the effects of excessive digital device use in teenagers. Excessive use is linked to psychiatric problems, musculoskeletal discomfort and sleep disruption.

I143.best_result: Random Forest, Decision Tree and Gradient Boosting (best classification)
I143.summary_en: Predicts student stress levels using a dataset of almost 20,000 entries (age, gender, family income, CGPA, academic pressure) and six classifiers. Random Forest, Decision Tree and Gradient Boosting show superior performance.

I144.summary_en: Reviews the integration of advanced analytics, wearables and predictive models into university physical fitness testing. It does not address mental health.

I145.summary_en: Develops machine learning models to identify student stress factors by combining a Kaggle dataset with directly collected samples, and implements a real-time detection interface with recommendations. No metrics are reported.

I146.summary_en: Detects stress, anxiety and depression in private university students in Bangladesh using validated questionnaires on sleep, study habits and digital activity, with SAINT, TabNet, NODE, CatBoost and a rank-based ensemble. CatBoost reaches 99.55% accuracy and the ensemble maintains 98%.

I147.summary_en: Proposes the design of an evaluation index system for college students' physical health quality supported by IoT, AI and big data. It does not address mental health or report results.

I148.screening_reason: abstract focused on emotion generation; no data or results
I148.summary_en: Explores GAN-based emotion representation from social media behavior to identify psychological health and personality traits of college students for early warning. No data or results are described.

I149.summary_en: Analyses student sentiment about college mental health support using public Student Voice Survey data, building the SMILE-College dataset and comparing traditional ML with LLMs. GPT-3.5 and BERT perform best.

I150.summary_en: Studies depression in 834 engineering and medical students in Bangladesh using questionnaires, selecting 16 features with t-tests and Fisher's exact test and classifying with SVM. Metric values are not reported.

I151.summary_en: Outlines an MRI image response model with SVM and data mining to analyse the impact of physical training on students' physical and mental health. Only a simulation-based verification is mentioned, without data or results.

I152.summary_en: Proposes a heterogeneous graph neural network with attention over multi-source data (text, behavior, physiology) to identify student psychological risk, with SHAP for personalized profiles. The multimodal model reaches 89.2% accuracy and physiological features are the most informative.

I153.summary_en: Detects depression in college students from PHQ-9 responses and a questionnaire, comparing Logistic Regression, XGBoost, SVM and Random Forest. Random Forest performs best (98% accuracy, F1 98.68%).

I154.screening_reason: general health/quality of life, no clear mental health focus
I154.summary_en: Describes a machine-learning-based information and analytics system to assess factors affecting students' health and quality of life and build a digital health profile. No data or results are reported.

I155.summary_en: Identifies factors of positive mental health in junior and senior high school students from questionnaire data using fusion-based feature selection and machine learning classifiers. The best classifier reaches an F1-score of 0.844.

I156.summary_en: Develops a campus physical health test system embedding a C4.5 decision tree to analyse college sports test data. Lung capacity emerges as the most important factor.

I157.screening_reason: counselor management, not student mental health
I157.summary_en: Proposes a data mining model and intelligent management system for college counselor teams in China. It does not address mental health or report results.

I158.summary_en: Proposes a BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism and parameter optimization, sensitive to emotional text, for early detection of college students' mental health problems. The enhanced model outperforms standard models in accuracy, recall and F1, but no data or metric values are reported.

I159.summary_en: Builds a social anxiety item bank and computerized adaptive test for college students using IRT analyses within an SQL sequence mining framework, combined with VR-based assessment. VR assessment results are reported to be closer to self-assessment scales and daily life.

I160.summary_en: Studies strategies to improve the physical fitness of art college students using smart bracelets, an Android system and a data mining model. It does not address mental health; performance is only said to be validated.

I161.screening_reason: mixed population (students and professionals); instrument validation with statistics
I161.best_result: Linear regression adjusted R² 52.5%; IRT reliability 0.891
I161.summary_en: Develops and validates BOOST, a subjective well-being instrument, with 333 university students and professionals mainly from the United States and India, using IRT and linear regression. Reliability is 0.891, the six attributes explain 52.5% of well-being, and well-being differs by country and field of study.

I162.summary_en: Predicts college dropout using academic, demographic and socioeconomic features combined in an ensemble with SVM. The model reaches 91.61% accuracy.

I163.summary_en: Presents Tampu, a mobile-wearable system that detects anxiety episodes in university students from heart rate, HRV and SpO2 with an on-device machine learning model, piloted for 15 days with 30 students (2,574 records). The model reaches 86.7% accuracy and usability is high (SUS 87/100).

I164.best_result: DT-MTPSO (better F1 than traditional Decision Tree)
I164.summary_en: Designs an architecture to predict college students' psychological health from multi-source data (operation support system, educational and questionnaire data) with a decision tree optimized by multiple-target particle swarm optimization. It outperforms a traditional decision tree in F1 and reveals links between behavior and psychological health.

I165.summary_en: Proposes an explainable deep learning framework with multi-head attention fusing behavioral, academic, psychological and social media data, with LIME and Grad-CAM, tested on 4,287 students. It achieves 92.35% accuracy in psychological risk detection, outperforming existing multimodal fusion models by 4.9-5.0%.

I166.summary_en: Predicts student depression from non-clinical demographic, academic, lifestyle, social, financial and emotional data, comparing ten supervised models with SMOTE. XGBoost achieves ROC AUC 0.95, and SHAP highlights academic pressure, poor sleep, financial difficulties and low social support.

I167.summary_en: Classifies psychological stress in higher education students using 801 student records and five algorithms (RF, NB, KNN, SVM, LR). Logistic Regression performs best (94.56% accuracy, macro AUC 99.54).

I168.summary_en: Compares two chatbot implementations (Streamlit/Ngrok vs Botpress) using rule-based systems and machine learning to provide emotional support to college students, evaluated on throughput, latency and reliability. No quantitative results are reported.

I169.summary_en: Develops a big-data psychological crisis intervention platform for higher vocational students that integrates scattered campus data to track psychological state and behavior. No method details or results are reported.

I170.summary_en: Proposes an improved gated recurrent unit (IGRU) to identify psychological stress in college engineering students from a Likert questionnaire administered to 127 students. IGRU reaches 98.81% accuracy and 96.32% F1, outperforming GRU.

I171.screening_reason: physical education learning, not mental health
I171.summary_en: Designs a data mining platform to analyse college students' physical education learning outcomes to support teaching diagnosis. It does not address mental health.

I172.summary_en: Discusses big-data-based intervention modes for Internet addiction among college students using a large survey and case interviews at UESTC (China), identifying main factors with chi-square tests. Specific results are not reported.

I173.summary_en: Proposes DBHP-DSCN, a sparse autoencoder framework that encodes high-dimensional student activity and behavior data to detect early signs of stress, anxiety or depression. It is reported to detect behavioral anomalies better than conventional methods, without metrics or data details.

I174.screening_reason: student engagement assessment, not mental health
I174.summary_en: Exploratory literature review mapping how student engagement is assessed in technology-enhanced learning, covering self-reports, learning analytics and ethics. It identifies gaps at the intersection of engagement, digital well-being and ethics.

I175.summary_en: Applies a decision tree algorithm to evaluate college students' mental health and predict depression, anxiety and suicidal ideation, feeding results back to counsellors. The abstract is incoherent and reports no data or results.

I176.summary_en: Proposes an education evaluation system for Chinese higher vocational colleges based on Internet, big data and AI technologies. It does not address mental health.

I177.summary_en: Presents EMHC, which classifies students from several universities in India's NCR region into good, moderate or bad mental health using categorical and sentiment attributes collected via a web application, with DeepFace, K-means and a support vector classifier. No performance results are reported.

I178.best_result: SVM with Dolphin optimization accuracy 0.998, F1 0.99
I178.summary_en: Proposes an SVM combined with Dolphin optimization to predict students' mental stress using Kaggle's Student Mental Health dataset (over 1,000 records). It reaches 0.998 accuracy and 0.99 F1, outperforming traditional algorithms.

I179.summary_en: Develops a system to help teachers identify students at mental health risk in Bangladesh using a culturally tailored survey and four classifiers. Logistic Regression performs best (94% accuracy), ahead of SVC and Random Forest (81%) and XGBoost (75%).

I180.best_result: Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM accuracy >97%
I180.summary_en: Detects student depression from 27,000 entries with demographic, academic, lifestyle and psychological characteristics, comparing six models with SMOTE balancing. Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM exceed 97% accuracy.

I181.screening_reason: mixed population (students and teachers); incoherent review
I181.summary_en: Reviews the use of machine learning (SVM, KNN, K-means) to analyse mental stress in students and teachers and motivates mental health apps. The abstract is loosely structured and reports no synthesis results.

I182.summary_en: Proposes WVES, a weighted voting ensemble, to predict depression levels using a public dataset collected at the International Islamic University Malaysia. It achieves 91% accuracy in 10-fold stratified cross-validation, outperforming traditional baselines.

I183.best_result: SVM best accuracy (pre-test); KNN best accuracy (post-test)
I183.summary_en: Examines the correlation between perceived stress (PSS) and sleep quality (PSQI) in the public StudentLife dataset and classifies well-being as good, average or bad with DT, SVM and KNN. Linear regression shows a significant association; SVM performs best on pre-test and KNN on post-test data.

I184.summary_en: Analyses students' online mobile game addiction level based on depression, social anxiety and loneliness using Logistic Regression, Ridge Regression and SVM. SVM achieves the highest accuracy (91.68%); the data are not described.

I185.summary_en: Proposes Fed-CBA, a federated CNN-BiLSTM-attention framework with differential privacy integrating LMS, EMA surveys, wearables and lifestyle data to predict university students' mental health risks, with SHAP and LIME. It outperforms DNN, CNN and LSTM and improves fairness, without reported metric values.

I186.summary_en: Predicts low well-being and academic risk from gaming behavior in 267 Saudi university students (WHO-5, GAD-7, IGDS9-SF) with logistic regression, random forest and clustering. Predictive accuracy is modest (ROC-AUC ≈0.52 for well-being), while clustering identifies three gamer typologies differing in well-being, gaming disorder and sleep.

I187.summary_en: Presents Jousvex, a tool combining a multilayer perceptron trained on the public Student Lifestyle dataset with an LLM to predict and communicate academic stress levels in university students. The MLP reaches 97% accuracy, outperforming traditional classifiers.

I188.summary_en: Screens college students for depression and social anxiety using text message metadata features (reply latency, consecutive messages, conversation ratio) and machine learning. Tree ensembles reach balanced accuracy 0.81 for depression and 0.78 for social anxiety.

I189.summary_en: Proposes an automated psychological behavior analysis framework to identify student depressive tendencies with LDA, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest. Models reach up to 86% accuracy; the data are not described.

I190.summary_en: Describes the "Mindfulness" app for university students combining facial emotion recognition (YOLOv8), social media content analysis and AI to detect and mitigate stress and anxiety. The emotion recognition component reaches 91.4% accuracy.

I191.summary_en: Presents BlissBot, a chatbot using NLP and machine learning to provide mental health education, resources and support to individuals. No data or results are reported.

I192.best_result: RF, KNN and SVM about 95% accuracy (reviewed studies)
I192.summary_en: PRISMA systematic review of machine learning for stress detection in university students (2019-2024), selecting 38 of 249 articles. Supervised models such as RF, KNN and SVM are the most common and effective (about 95% accuracy), and physiological datasets such as WESAD are frequent sources.

I193.summary_en: Presents a hybrid pipeline (KNN imputation, SMOTE-ENN, PCA) with RF, SVM, MLP and stacking/voting ensembles to detect anxiety, depression and stress from self-report questionnaires of 2,028 university students. Stacking achieves 100%, 99.69% and 99.18% accuracy, respectively.

I194.summary_en: Introduces MindWell Solace, a Flask chatbot that detects potential mental disorders in college students through symptom-based conversations using a Random Forest classifier and notifies counsellors. No performance results are reported.

I195.summary_en: Presents MindSync, an AI-powered web study companion that tracks student emotions, generates schedules and provides motivational messages. It reports 89.4% accuracy and a 34.2% schedule improvement, without describing data or method.

I196.summary_en: Introduces Merrytopia, a well-being platform combining NLP/ML sentiment analysis of journaling with Unity virtual environments for mindfulness. No evaluation results are reported.

I197.summary_en: Builds an explainable pipeline with Random Forest and SHAP to predict student dropout using data from a Brazilian public higher education institution. It identifies the weight of academic, age and sociodemographic factors, without reporting metrics.

I198.summary_en: Proposes a meta-heuristic feature selector (Henon-enabled Dwarf Mongoose) with a stacked RF, KNN and SVM framework to predict students' stress levels. The RF-SVM model reaches 0.988 accuracy and 0.98 F1; the data are not described.

I199.summary_en: Develops a student mental health risk prediction model combining natural language processing and graph neural networks on a constructed campus social interaction dataset. The abstract outlines the study structure without reporting results.

I200.summary_en: Predicts academic burnout risk in 1,250 university students from an online survey on workload, stress, social interaction and lifestyle, comparing XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM and an Explainable Boosting Machine. XGBoost achieves 99.47% accuracy and EBM 97.87%; workload perception and stress are the strongest predictors.

I201.summary_en: Proposes a BiLSTM with self-attention to classify university students into mental health risk categories using cross-sectional survey data, with MICE imputation, SMOTE and Boruta/stepwise feature selection. The model reaches 0.978 accuracy, outperforming a DNN.

I202.summary_en: Proposes an ensemble of SVM, Random Forest and Extreme Learning Machine for health early warning in college students using the public Student-Health-Data dataset with physiological, psychological and behavioral indicators. It achieves 97.8% accuracy and AUC-ROC 0.986.

I203.best_result: GCN (higher accuracy than psychological scale and other ML algorithms)
I203.summary_en: Identifies college students in psychological crisis with a graph convolutional network using psychological questionnaire data and relationship information among students. The GCN outperforms the psychological scale and other machine learning algorithms in recognition accuracy.

I204.summary_en: Compares eight classifiers for three-level mental health risk detection on a public multimodal student dataset with early fusion of physiological, emotional, behavioral and contextual features. Logistic Regression reaches 98.4% accuracy but XGBoost is best in macro-F1 (0.82); all models detect the high-risk class poorly and emotional and behavioral modalities dominate.

I205.summary_en: Predicts academic stress of students during COVID-19 emergency remote learning from survey data on study time, social media and health, using Naive Bayes, Random Forest and ANN. No metric values or best model are reported.

I206.screening_reason: general college chatbot, not mental health
I206.summary_en: Case study on designing a college chatbot on Microsoft Azure using NLP to answer inquiries of students, faculty and staff. It does not address mental health.

I207.summary_en: Describes a voice assistant AI bot using NLP and machine learning to provide students with mental health support and career guidance. No data or results are reported.

I208.screening_reason: classical statistics; physical self-concept only indirectly related to mental health
I208.summary_en: Compares physical self-concept between college athletes and non-athletes and across four sports teams using Pearson correlation and linear regression. Athletes score significantly higher, and age correlates positively with physical self-concept in volleyball and softball players.

I209.summary_en: Designs a machine learning model to detect Internet addiction in teenage and university students from behavioral features, comparing five algorithms. Random Forest reaches 83% accuracy for university students and SVM 96% for teenagers.

I210.summary_en: Predicts student academic performance in online learning during COVID-19 using a questionnaire-based dataset and four classifiers. It notes that excessive use of electronic devices harmed academic performance and mental health, without reporting metrics.

I211.screening_reason: general essay on AI in classroom management
I211.summary_en: Discusses AI and machine learning applications in classroom management and behavior analysis, including attendance tracking, engagement monitoring and sentiment analysis to detect stress or anxiety. No empirical data or results are reported.

I212.summary_en: Proposes a sentiment-analysis chatbot for early detection of depression in university students in Peru using PHQ-9 items reformulated as open-ended questions. Gradient Boosting achieves 0.81 accuracy.

I213.summary_en: Develops a cloud-based college psychological counseling platform that uses k-means clustering to group students with different types of psychological problems. Psychological recovery is reported to increase by 7.3%.

I214.screening_reason: review of survey instruments, no data analytics or ML
I214.summary_en: Work-in-progress scoping review of survey instruments used to assess mental health of STEM graduate students across five databases, with 29 studies included so far. Only preliminary findings are provided.

I215.summary_en: Analyses factors influencing student mental health using data augmentation, chi-square and Pearson correlation, refining the sample to the 18-26 age group, and applies Random Forest and Naive Bayes. Random Forest reaches 75.85% accuracy versus 71.68% for Naive Bayes.

I216.summary_en: Applies adaptive active learning with KNN, LR, XGBoost, NB and RF to predict student anxiety levels on two student behavior datasets. Active-learning LR scores 0.61 and RF 0.60 on the first dataset, and RF reaches 0.83 accuracy on the second.

I217.summary_en: Proposes a Puzzle Optimization Algorithm with an artificial neural network to predict student physical health assessment. POA-ANN reaches 0.973 accuracy and 0.965 F1.

I218.summary_en: Builds a Random Forest system to classify gadget addiction risk (low, moderate, high) in over 3,450 Indian students from a Google Form questionnaire on behavioral and psychological patterns, integrated into a web app. The model reaches 91.40% accuracy and 91.22% F1.

I219.summary_en: Proposes an AIoT wearable band that monitors heart rate, body temperature and physical activity and analyses the data in the cloud with machine learning to detect student stress. Deep learning models reach a maximum accuracy of 94.4%.

I220.summary_en: Proposes an attention-GRU framework with federated learning and differential privacy fusing wearable, campus card and anonymous social platform data to detect psychological fluctuations and abnormal behavior, trained on 30 days of data from 2,000 students (simulated and SWELL-KW). F1 improves by 12.5% over single-modal LSTM and drops only 2.3% under strong privacy.

I221.summary_en: Proposes a neural network model processing speech, facial expressions and behavioral measures with sentiment analysis to identify stress, anxiety and depression levels in college students. It reports 96% accuracy on real student datasets, without describing them.

I222.summary_en: Predicts student mental health risk from academic data comparing Decision Tree, Random Forest and SVC with feature selection and GridSearchCV tuning. Random Forest performs best (73.98% accuracy).

I223.screening_reason: financial stress and retention; partial mental health relevance
I223.summary_en: Predicts student financial stress and dropout risk using Decision Trees, LightGBM, KNN, ANN and a voting classifier with ADASYN oversampling. LightGBM performs best (up to 91.16% accuracy).

I224.summary_en: Examines the relationship between mental health factors (pressure, anxiety, stress, among others) and academic performance, using Eclat to find frequent patterns and Naive Bayes to predict performance, with a web platform. No metrics are reported.

I225.summary_en: Presents an AI student stress detection and recommendation system that classifies distress and eustress from self-reported indicators, behaviors and academic habits with supervised models and suggests personalized interventions. No quantitative results are reported.

I226.screening_reason: abstract describes a management system without analytics despite the title
I226.summary_en: Designs a college psychological education and counseling management system (Java, SSH, MySQL) with online testing and file management modules. Despite the deep learning title, no analytic method or results are described.

I227.screening_reason: IoT review; ML analytics not explicit
I227.summary_en: Reviews IoT use in schools with a focus on student well-being, performance, parental support and management, and proposes an early IoT architecture. No empirical results are reported.

I228.screening_reason: topic modeling of posts; mental health not the main outcome
I228.summary_en: Applies LDA topic modeling to Facebook confession page posts from 14 Philippine universities (2018-2022). It identifies two general and five underlying topics, such as confessing vulnerabilities and ranting about daily struggles, with "mental-health" among frequent co-occurring terms.

I229.screening_reason: review of GenAI student support; well-being only one domain
I229.summary_en: Structured literature review of generative AI in higher education student support across academic support, pastoral care and well-being, inclusivity, analytics and employability. Impact depends on pedagogical integration and hybrid human-AI models.

I230.summary_en: Predicts university students' mental health risk levels from IoT environmental sensing data (temperature, air quality, noise, crowding) and modeled indicators (stress, sleep, mood). A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest and SVM reaches 98% accuracy.

I231.screening_reason: mobile app without data analytics or ML
I231.summary_en: Proposes "Deep Sleep", a mobile app with psychologist monitoring and PSQI-based sleep quality assessment for university students, validated with 2 psychologists and 30 students. Poor sleepers decrease by 20% and user satisfaction is 79.63%.

I232.summary_en: Identifies mental health risk in 266 undergraduates at a Thai university using survey behavioral data, SMOTE, Random Forest, XGBoost and deep learning, plus correlation analysis and K-means. XGBoost performs best (90.60% accuracy, F1 83.90%) and clustering reveals subgroups of at-risk students.

I233.summary_en: Compares machine learning and deep learning models to predict student mental health concerns using 30 Google Form samples with 13 psychological and emotional indicators. CNN achieves the highest accuracy (87.12%), followed by Random Forest (85.52%).

I234.screening_reason: online platform without data analytics or ML
I234.summary_en: Proposes an Internet-based psychology self-service platform that allocates psychological resources to college students in the post-epidemic era. No analytics or results are reported.
